title: Linings and mesenteries

objective.text: Explain how the body-cavity linings and the mesenteries form.

body.general: Why do your gut and lungs slide smoothly inside you? Each cavity has a thin, slippery lining, a serous membrane [f1]. The outer mesoderm sheet lines the cavity walls [f1]. The inner sheet covers the organs [f2]. The two are one continuous layer, folded back where each organ attaches, like a fist pushed into a balloon [f3]. The gut hangs from the back wall in a double sheet, the dorsal mesentery [f4]. Mesenteries carry the gut's blood vessels and nerves [f6]. A front sheet, the ventral mesentery, holds only a short stretch near the stomach [f7].
body.mbbs: Some parietal-layer cells become mesothelium, the parietal peritoneum, pleura and pericardium lining the cavity walls [f1]. Some visceral-layer cells form the visceral layer covering the abdominal organs, lungs and heart [f2]. The two layers are continuous at each organ's root, like a fist in a balloon [f3]. The dorsal mesentery is a double layer of peritoneum suspending the gut from the dorsal body wall [f4]. It runs from the caudal foregut to the end of the hindgut [f5]. Mesenteries carry blood vessels, nerves and lymphatics to the organs [f6]. The ventral mesentery exists only from the lower oesophagus and stomach to the upper duodenum [f7]. It comes from thinning of septum transversum mesoderm, the plate below the heart [f8].

facts.text: Some cells of the parietal layer become mesothelium: the parietal layer of the peritoneum, pleura and pericardium that lines the cavity walls.
facts.note: R06: coelomic surface cells become the permanent serous membranes

facts.text: Some cells of the visceral layer become the visceral layer of serous membrane covering the abdominal organs, lungs and heart.
facts.note: R06: lung mesenchyme and its outer mesothelium come from the coelomic wall

facts.text: The parietal and visceral layers are continuous with each other at each organ's root, like a fist pushed into a balloon.
The dorsal mesentery is a double layer of peritoneum that hangs the gut from the dorsal body wall.
facts.note: R05ao: continuous double layer, widest at stomach and duodenum

facts.text: In the book the dorsal mesentery runs from the caudal foregut to the end of the hindgut.
facts.note: R05ao counts it from pharynx to anus, a wider definition, not used

facts.text: Mesenteries carry blood vessels, nerves and lymphatics to the organs.
The ventral mesentery exists only from the caudal foregut (lower oesophagus and stomach) to the upper duodenum.
The ventral mesentery comes from thinning of the mesoderm of the septum transversum.

misconceptions.wrong: The parietal and visceral peritoneum are two separate sacs.
misconceptions.right: They are one continuous layer, folded back at each organ's root, like a fist in a balloon.

misconceptions.wrong: The ventral mesentery runs the whole length of the gut.
misconceptions.right: It exists only from the lower oesophagus and stomach to the upper duodenum; the dorsal mesentery runs much further.

checks.prompt: How are the parietal and visceral peritoneum related?
options: Two separate sacs that never meet
One continuous layer, folded back at each organ's root
The visceral layer grows out of the gut's endoderm
The parietal layer comes from the ectoderm
checks.why: Both come from lateral plate mesoderm and meet at the organ's root, like a fist in a balloon.

checks.prompt: Which stretch of gut has a ventral mesentery?
options: The whole gut, from mouth to anus
Lower oesophagus, stomach and upper duodenum
checks.why: The ventral mesentery comes from the septum transversum, so it exists only at the caudal foregut and upper duodenum.

checks.prompt: Which lining comes from the parietal layer of mesoderm?
options: The peritoneum lining the belly wall
The inner lining of the gut
checks.why: Parietal-layer cells line the cavity walls; visceral-layer cells cover the organs; the gut's inner lining is endoderm.

adult: These become the adult peritoneum, pleura and pericardium, and the mesenteries that carry the gut's vessels and nerves [f1,f2,f6].

remember.q: What lines the cavity walls, and what covers the organs?
remember.a: Parietal-layer mesothelium lines the walls; visceral-layer cells cover the organs [f1,f2].
A double layer of peritoneum hanging the gut from the dorsal body wall [f4].

remember.q: Where does the ventral mesentery exist, and where does it come from?
remember.a: Only lower oesophagus, stomach and upper duodenum; from thinning septum transversum mesoderm [f7,f8].
